match_note: arXiv v1 is dated 14 Feb 2026, the day after the second rebuttal (13 Feb 2026), so it appears to be the post-revision manuscript. Several signs confirm this. v1 uses 'spontaneous mode' and f_spon, where the reviewed text used 'auto-oscillation' and f_auto. It includes the Suhl references [31,32] that R1 requested. It shows red-highlighted inserted text ('as shown in 2(a)'; the P_spon definition after Eq. 2). Text the rebuttals say was removed is absent: 'well-defined selecting rules', the tunability ratio, omega notation, 'second probe signal', and the 'pump filtered' sentence. The reviewed version therefore differed from v1 in wording and in some figure details (labels in Fig. 1a/3a, lines in Fig. 1d/2b). The core data and claims appear the same.

concerns.quote: Equations (1) and (2) can be found in [9] and originally deduced for STNO ... for the lowest mode with k = 0. ... the validity of the use of (1) and (2) should be explicitly stated
concerns.summary: The STNO phase-locking model (Eqs. 1-2), derived for a k=0 mode, is applied to k≠0 parametrically generated modes without justification.

concerns.quote: the role of surface spin wave nonreciprocity (NR) does not well discussed... it will be better to indicate mutual orientation of the wave vector and the magnetic field
concerns.summary: The role of Damon-Eshbach nonreciprocity and the field/wavevector orientation used are not clearly explained.

concerns.quote: Consider adding an example of measured spectra for different magnetic field directions at least at supplementary.
concerns.summary: Requests spectra measured for other field directions to show the nonreciprocity dependence.

concerns.quote: What types of NR were found (amplitude or frequency)? Can amplitude NR lead to frequency NR due to nonisochronicity
concerns.summary: Asks whether the nonreciprocity is in amplitude or frequency, and whether nonlinear frequency shift could convert one into the other.

concerns.quote: there is also an upper limit. What is its physical reason?
concerns.summary: The physical origin of the upper pump-power bound for the spontaneous peak is not explained.

concerns.quote: The text lacks the references to classical works on magnetization parametric dynamics. Consider citing original works by for example Suhl.
concerns.summary: Classical references on parametric magnetization dynamics (Suhl) are missing.

concerns.quote: If possible, indicate the direction of the external magnetic field in Fig. 1a and Fig. 3a
concerns.summary: Field direction should be marked in the schematics of Figs. 1a and 3a.

concerns.quote: There is no refence in the text to Fig.1(d)... no reference to a Fig.3(f) and 3(h)... What is hprobe and Posc?
concerns.summary: Some figure panels are never cited in the text, and the symbols h_probe and P_osc are undefined.

concerns.quote: Some abbreviations are defined more than once (e.g., VNA, SA).
concerns.summary: Some abbreviations are defined more than once.

concerns.quote: It is better to reformulate the following sentence to avoid the use of repeated commas.
concerns.summary: The intro sentence on 2k mode amplitude, linewidth and Q factor should be rewritten.

concerns.quote: There are no definitions of the quantities k_par and k_per in Figure S4... How do they relate to the quantity k in Fig. 1(b)?
concerns.summary: Fig. S4 has undefined wavevector components, a wrong color label and cumbersome axis units.

concerns.quote: Perhaps it is not worth introducing the circular frequencies ω at all... designate the frequencies along the horizontal axes of Figures 5(a) and 5(i) in the same way
concerns.summary: Notation for frequencies is inconsistent (ω vs f) in the text and Fig. 5.

concerns.quote: The general idea is not particularly novel, and the authors could/should articulate the novelty aspect of their work better.
concerns.summary: Four-wave-mixing generation and amplification is not a new idea, and the novelty is poorly articulated.

concerns.quote: The discussion of the "well-defined selecting rules" implies that the manuscript solved the problem... It is not quite clear what rules (or perhaps rather constraints?) are implied.
concerns.summary: The claimed 'well-defined selection rules' for 4WM are never specified.

concerns.quote: "strictly following the theoretical prediction". Such prediction has not been properly elaborated in the manuscript.
concerns.summary: A claimed agreement with theory is asserted without the theory being presented.

concerns.quote: "Here f_idler is not measured.." but isn't it measured later in text?
concerns.summary: The statement that the idler is not measured contradicts its later observation.

concerns.quote: Is \Delta f_auto the tunability window? Why is the tunability ratio important? How is it increasing at lower f_pump?? And how is it related to auto-oscillations disappearing below the 5.39GHz pump?
concerns.summary: The tunability-ratio analysis and its frequency dependence are unclear and unexplained.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: How is it possible that the idler mode's frequency falls below the Kittel mode?
concerns.summary: The inferred idler frequencies lie below the Kittel mode, which conflicts with the proposed quasi-k=0 idler picture.

concerns.quote: f_idler happens to be near k=0 and cannot go lower... how does it make the 4WM process robust? Is it implied that a f-k minimum at k=0 increases the number of possible scattering states
concerns.summary: The claim that the 4WM process is robust lacks a physical explanation.

concerns.quote: "The narrow linewidth shows that … the selection rule is confined in the weak nonlinearity regime". This sentence needs to be elaborated.
concerns.summary: The link between narrow linewidth and the 4WM selection rule is unexplained.

concerns.quote: It's probably not the "second" probe signal, but simply a probe signal (that is in addition to the pump signal).
concerns.summary: Calling the probe a 'second probe signal' is misleading, here and in the abstract and intro.

concerns.quote: Does the observed mode attraction rigorously prove phase-locking? Please explain and provide references ([9]?).
concerns.summary: Mode attraction alone may not prove true phase-locking.

concerns.quote: Also the harmonic should be better explained.
concerns.summary: The origin of the harmonic mode in the phase-locking data is not explained.

concerns.quote: Eq.1 is "nice" but it does not fit the entire scope of the data.
concerns.summary: The Adler-type fit (Eq. 1) does not describe all of the phase-locking data.

concerns.quote: Has the f-k been measured and calculated (Supplemental Section 4 does not seem sufficient / clearly representative)? Do both energy conservation and k conservation of the 4WM process check out?
concerns.summary: No measured or calculated dispersion confirms that both energy and momentum conservation hold for the proposed 4WM.

concerns.quote: Is the phase-locked oscillation within the locking band actually visible in the SA measurements? Please explain.
concerns.summary: Asks whether the locked state is directly seen in the spectrum-analyzer data.

concerns.quote: The explanation for the irregular appearance of the idler mode does not seem very solid.
concerns.summary: The idler appears only under some conditions, and the explanation for this is weak.

concerns.quote: would the process not be excited symmetrically for positive and negative k? With the film thickness of only 100nm, this should not be a problem for detecting even in the Damon Eshbach geometry?
concerns.summary: The 4WM should populate both ±k, and a 100 nm film should make the idler detectable, so the non-detection is puzzling.

concerns.quote: "In contrast, our magnon parametric amplification requires only pump…". Please address the presence of thermal magnons.
concerns.summary: Thermal magnons may act as an effective second input in the claimed single-pump amplification.

concerns.quote: "... avoids Joule heating" or reduces it (consider antenna)?
concerns.summary: The claim of avoiding Joule heating is overstated given antenna heating.

concerns.quote: "Consequently, the amplified magnon signal does not preserve…". This sentence is in (apparent?) contradiction with the preceding one.
concerns.summary: The comparison with 3WM amplification and phase preservation is self-contradictory.

concerns.quote: If "identification of a robust 4WM condition …" is in fact the main novelty of the manuscript, it needs to be expanded and better discussed.
concerns.summary: The claimed main novelty (a robust 4WM condition) is not sufficiently developed.

concerns.quote: are these refs truly spin-torque or effectively a thermal torque? E.g. [Nat. Commun. 8, 117 (2017)] is strictly speaking also a 4WM. There have also been reports of non-degenerate 3WM with amplification
concerns.summary: Prior-work characterization is inaccurate and misses relevant 4WM/thermal-torque and non-degenerate 3WM amplification reports.

concerns.quote: the concept of the idler mode should be explained or redescribed, instead of simply being dropped in the intro section.
concerns.summary: The idler mode and related sentences in the intro and results are introduced unclearly.

concerns.quote: explain "clearly compensated frequency shifts"
concerns.summary: The phrase about compensated frequency shifts of spon and idler needs explanation.

concerns.quote: "such difference" - unclear choice of the wording.
concerns.summary: The wording 'such difference' is unclear.

concerns.quote: It would be great to see in all plots additional horizontal or vertical lines that represent the pertinent complementary frequency of the 4WM process
concerns.summary: Plots should mark the complementary 4WM frequencies.

concerns.quote: The term "phase autonomous" is precise but should be introduced early in the paper for the general reader.
concerns.summary: The term 'phase autonomous' should be defined early.

concerns.quote: There are also a few instances of incorrect grammar, choice of preposition, missing words, etc.
concerns.summary: Various wording and grammar fixes are needed (reproductivity, measured/generated, 'constant increase', the 40 dB sentence, band structure, sub-microwave CPW, 'photon' in the Fig. 1 caption).

later_concerns.quote: If the pumping is filtered, i.e., eliminated, then how can nonlinear spin waves occur in the sample at all?
later_concerns.summary: The newly added statement about filtering the pump is physically confusing.

later_concerns.quote: hprobe is still not explained in the text and is present in the caption to Fig.3.
later_concerns.summary: h_probe remains undefined in the Fig. 3 caption.

later_concerns.quote: The authors did not replace fauto with fspon. If the isofrequency curves for fpump are shown in orange... why is the fpump icon yellow and lies on the red curve?
later_concerns.summary: Fig. S4 labels and colors are still inconsistent.

later_concerns.quote: There is still no reference to Fig.2 (a).
later_concerns.summary: Fig. 2(a) is not cited in the text.

first_round.quote: The work “Magnonic spontaneous oscillation induced by parametric pumping” looks solid and is well written, and may be accepted for publication after the revision.
The general idea is not particularly novel, and the authors could/should articulate the novelty aspect of their work better... their interpretation could benefit from more rigor and depth

recommendations.note: The file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal, so the first round is Version 0. Neither referee states a recommendation category in round 1, so both are inferred. R1 calls the work solid and acceptable 'after the revision'. R1's requests are mostly clarifications, labels, references and figure fixes, plus one optional supplementary dataset, so this reads as minor revision. R2 finds the results interesting but questions the novelty. R2 also asks for substantially more rigorous interpretation: whether the f-k dispersion was measured or calculated, whether energy and momentum conservation check out, whether phase-locking is rigorously proven, and why the idler mode appears irregularly. That points to major revision. Later rounds are not used for the ratings: R1 recommended publication 'after minor revisions and corrections' in Version 1 and then publication in Version 2. R2's Version 1 report is blank and R2 does not appear in Version 2.
recommendations.label: contested
